title: Normalized auction schedule definition (standalone auctionhouse table)
description: Contract for one normalized auction schedule entry: exactly one committed entry of the standalone `config/auctionhouse.json` table. The committed `uuid` stays the JSON string and becomes legacy_id verbatim (rule A1); `interval` is preserved in its committed unit, minutes, and is NOT converted (rule A2); `unit` resolves against the normalized units package and the resolved display name is carried (rule A3); `betPrice` is carried verbatim beside the measured record that it has zero consumers in the preserved server (rule A4). Every transformation is listed in x-coercion-ruleset: a coercion that cannot be listed is not permitted. The legacy module is read as text only and never imported or executed.

rules.note: The committed uuid is already a JSON string and becomes legacy_id verbatim. It is NOT parsed into an integer: the legacy module keys its state document by that value (auctions.py:106) and the committed table declares it quoted, so an integer would claim a type the source does not carry.
Carried alongside legacy_id so the round-trip comparison covers the committed key verbatim and so a reader never has to infer it.
The committed unit id is carried as the native integer the source commits.
Cross-domain reference edge: the decimal form of the committed integer, matched against the normalized units legacy_id set. Unresolvable ids are recorded unresolved, never replaced.
The display name carried by the resolved normalized unit entry, or null when the id does not resolve. No name is invented, substituted or defaulted.
Whether unit_ref is present in the normalized units legacy-id set. Recorded rather than enforced: an unresolvable definition is still emitted, in committed order, and reported.
Committed verbatim. No level gate, threshold or reachability rule is derived; the corpus map level makes the committed level unreachable as a gate, which is a finding, not a normalization.

Committed verbatim in the committed unit, MINUTES. No conversion is performed here; the legacy module's single conversion (seconds = auction["interval"] * 60, auctions.py:76) belongs to the consuming client in one named function, and the factor 60 is deliberately not recorded as data in this package.
The constant label "minutes". This is the committed unit name, not a conversion and not a factor, so a reader cannot mistake the carried value for seconds.
Committed verbatim. It seeds the legacy state's beginPrice/currentPrice, and currentPrice is a pure function of the client-sent bid, so no price rule is derived.
Committed verbatim. It is added to the client-sent bid with no comparison operator anywhere in the module, so no increment check is derived.
Committed verbatim. It is written into the legacy state document at auctions.py:97 and auctions.py:137 and read nowhere.

Measured false beside the measurement that establishes it: the legacy module text holds zero whole-token occurrences of gold, coins, cash, wood, steel, oil, xp, mana, energy, cost or apply_resources and never calls apply_resources. The flag records an unconsumed committed price, not a meaningless one; no ordinal is claimed for it.

kind.note: Every committed entry maps to the single classification "auction".

source_file.note: The standalone committed file config/auctionhouse.json, which is NOT one of the 20 top-level keys of config/main.json, so no patch layering or mods pipeline applies to it.

source_layer.note: The constant "stored": this table is read as committed and never layered, replaced or patched.

content_version.note: sha256 over the committed auction config bytes and the committed normalized units bytes. Sources carry no version stamp; the fingerprint is the version record.

legacy_id.description: Committed uuid preserved verbatim as the committed JSON string (rule A1): not the decimal form of an integer, because the source declares it quoted and the legacy module keys its state document by it (auctions.py:106).

kind.description: Classification of the standalone auctionhouse domain: every committed entry maps to auction.

source_file.description: Origin file of the committed entry: the standalone committed auction table, which is outside the content census whose scope is the 20 top-level keys of config/main.json.

source_layer.description: Layering origin: stored. This table carries no patch layering and no mods pipeline, unlike every sibling builder that reads config/main.json.

content_version.description: Content fingerprint (sha256 over the committed auction config bytes and the committed normalized units bytes); sources carry no version stamp.

uuid.description: The committed uuid, carried verbatim as the committed JSON string alongside legacy_id (rule A1).

unit.description: Committed unit id, kept verbatim (rule A3); must resolve against the normalized units legacy-ID set for unit_resolved to be true.

unit_ref.description: Cross-domain unit reference: the decimal form of the committed integer unit id, validated against the normalized units legacy-ID set (rule A3).

unit_name.description: Display name carried by the resolved normalized unit entry, or null when the committed id does not resolve (rule A3). No name is invented or substituted.

unit_resolved.description: Whether unit_ref is present in the normalized units legacy-ID set (rule A3). Recorded rather than enforced: an unresolved definition is still emitted in committed order and reported.

level.description: Committed level, kept verbatim (rule A1). No gate, threshold or reachability rule is derived.

interval.description: Committed interval, kept verbatim in the committed unit MINUTES and NOT converted (rule A2). The legacy module's single conversion (seconds = auction["interval"] * 60, auctions.py:76) belongs to the consuming client, in one named function; no seconds or duration field is present and the factor 60 is not recorded as data.

interval_unit.description: The committed unit label for interval (rule A2). A unit name, not a conversion and not a factor.

price.description: Committed price, kept verbatim (rule A1). No price rule, clamp, floor or total is derived.

priceIncrement.description: Committed priceIncrement, kept verbatim (rule A1). No increment check is derived; the module holds zero comparison operators against its four price identifiers.

betPrice.description: Committed betPrice, kept verbatim (rule A4). Written into the legacy state document at auctions.py:97 and auctions.py:137 and read nowhere.

bet_price_consumed.description: Measured zero-consumer record for betPrice (rule A4): the legacy module text holds zero whole-token occurrences of gold, coins, cash, wood, steel, oil, xp, mana, energy, cost or apply_resources and never calls apply_resources. Const false because that measurement is re-measured from the committed module text on every build; a consumer appearing would fail the build rather than silently flip the flag.
